trending.name: lvgl
trending.author: kisvegabor
trending.sentence: Full-featured Graphics Library for Embedded Systems
trending.paragraph: Powerful and easy-to-use embedded GUI with many widgets, advanced visual effects (opacity, antialiasing, animations) and low memory requirements (16K RAM, 64K Flash).

trending.sentence: Multi-platform library for controlling dozens of different types of LEDs along with optimized math, effect, and noise functions.
trending.paragraph: FastLED is a fast, efficient, easy-to-use Arduino library for programming addressable LED strips and pixels such as WS2810, WS2811, LPD8806, Neopixel and more. FastLED also provides high-level math functions that can be used for generative art and graphics.

trending.sentence: A simple and efficient JSON library for embedded C++.
trending.paragraph: ⭐ 7124 stars on GitHub! Supports serialization, deserialization, MessagePack, streams, filtering, and more. Fully tested and documented.

trending.name: Blinker
trending.author: i3water
trending.sentence: Build a easy way for your IoT project.
trending.paragraph: Blinker library for embedded hardware. Support Arduino, ESP8266, ESP32, WiFi, BLE, MQTT.

trending.sentence: Send and receive infrared signals with multiple protocols
trending.paragraph: Currently included protocols: Denon / Sharp, JVC, LG,  NEC / Onkyo / Apple, Panasonic / Kaseikyo, RC5, RC6, Samsung, Sony, (Pronto), BangOlufsen, BoseWave, Lego, Whynter, FAST, MagiQuest, Velux, Universal Pulse Distance and Pulse Width.

trending.name: PubSubClient
trending.author: Nick O'Leary <nick.oleary@gmail.com>

It supports the latest MQTT 3.1.1 protocol and can be configured to use the older MQTT 3.1 if needed. It supports all Arduino Ethernet Client compatible hardware, including the Intel Galileo/Edison, ESP8266 and TI CC3000.

Features 64-bit microsecond precision, silicon hardware timer groups (TG0/TG1), high-resolution software timers (esp_timer), thread-safe FreeRTOS task callback dispatching, real-time jitter telemetry, pause/resume state control, and zero-overhead AyresTimeout and AyresStopwatch modules.

Sketches reduce to Pardalote.begin() / Pardalote.run(). Extensions for Servo, NeoPixel, Ultrasonic, IMU, and ESP32 Camera are included as opt-in headers.

hidden_gems.name: DS3502

hidden_gems.name: ESP32KeyBridge
hidden_gems.author: TANAKA Masayuki
hidden_gems.sentence: Bridge keyboard input to keyboard output on ESP32: remap, layers, macros, and layout conversion in between.
hidden_gems.paragraph: ESP32KeyBridge sits between a keyboard and the machine that reads it. It takes input from USB Host keyboards, mice, gamepads and MIDI devices, BLE HID keyboards and mice, GPIO switches, key matrices and rotary encoders, normalizes it into one key model, merges several inputs into one, applies single-step remapping across key kinds, momentary layers, disabled keys, text macros and keyboard layout conversion, and writes the result to USB Device HID, BLE HID, or a serial Print. The core is portable C++ with no Arduino, ESP-IDF or hardware dependency; adapters are header-only, so a sketch needs EspUsbHost, EspUsbDevice or EspBle only for the adapters it includes.

hidden_gems.name: ST77916_QSPI

hidden_gems.paragraph: Adafruit_GFX compatible, with dirty-rectangle partial updates, queued DMA, optional double buffering and a second-core push task, palettised and RGB565 blitting for GIF and MJPEG playback, alpha blending, anti-aliased primitives, and a p5.js-shaped drawing layer.

hidden_gems.name: AutonomniOTA
hidden_gems.author: matej Zvolsky
hidden_gems.sentence: Autonomous wireless background OTA flashing on a configurable ESP32 core.
hidden_gems.paragraph: This library spawns a FreeRTOS background task that independently handles ArduinoOTA and ElegantOTA. Wi-Fi, hostname, OTA services, task configuration and web server settings are configured in AutonomniOTA_Config.h, while user sketches only need to include AutonomniOTA.h.

hidden_gems.name: ESP-DOOM
hidden_gems.author: Rear Labs <rear-16@hotmail.com>
hidden_gems.sentence: Doom engine (doomgeneric) ported to ESP32/Arduino, with a custom PCM mixer, EQ and chiptune music synth.
hidden_gems.paragraph: Runs the Doom engine on ESP32-S3 boards with PSRAM. You provide three small interfaces (display, input, PCM audio) and a WAD file on SD/LittleFS; the library drives the game loop, renderer and its own software audio mixer (SFX + synthesized MUS music, with a runtime-tunable high-pass/limiter chain built for small speakers). Requires a board with at least ~6MB of free PSRAM today; see README for the memory budget and roadmap toward smaller targets.
